content:
Sara: quick sketch  proposing a tiny ops-layer to defragment VRAM by performing live region moves into a staging pool and remapping with a move token. not a wholesale allocator rewrite, more of a coordinator + optional forwarding.

Mike: curious  what's the win vs current evict+alloc? what's the latency profile we care about? :thinking:

Sara: today we evict then reallocate then rebuild KV cache which spikes tail. goal: nonblocking move + pointer swap to avoid full cache rebuild on hot paths.

Jia: safety question  what about kernels or CUDA streams with pointers into the old region? we need pin/hold semantics or a safe-fallback.

Sara: plan: move_region returns move_token + fence. two modes: ATOMIC (wait for pins to drop then swap) and FORWARDING (install ephemeral forwarding entry so old pointers still resolve for a short TTL).

Sam: forwarding helps correctness but adds lookup cost. can we keep forwarding off the fast-path most of the time?

Sara: yes  fast-path unchanged. forwarding consulted only on fault/remap slow-path. TTL small (single-digit ms) to bound cost.

Leo: allocator boundaries worry me. if allocators assume stable GPU VA, swapping underneath could break invariants.

Sara: that's why this is opt-in ops API. allocator must call move_region and mark region migrating. not a hidden runtime mutation.

Mike: show a minimal signature please.

Sara: pseudo:

```
move_region(src_va, size, dst_pool, flags) -> move_token
query_move(move_token) -> {state: pending|done|failed}
commit_move(move_token) -> success|retry
```

Jia: need idempotency and resumability. moves should persist tiny journal entries so they survive crash/restart.

Sara: agreed. move_token opaque but deterministic; runtime writes a compact nvlog entry per move to resume or reconcile.

Sam: telemetry hooks: move.latency_ms; move.forwarding_hits; move.atomic_vs_forwarding ratio; move.resumes_count.

Sara: adding metrics + histograms. also track compressed_size if compression used.

Mike: rollout strategy?

Sara: internal feature flag + unit/sim tests -> canary on dedicated -> expand to hosted once tail benefits verified.

Leo: test matrix: active CUDA kernels referencing moved region, long-lived pinned pages, multi-tenant mixing, crash-and-recovery while move in-flight.

dev-bot: CI: move-defrag-ops branch -> tests running (23/150)

Jia: thought: add optional COMPRESS_ON_MOVE flag. compress while copying to reduce dst footprint; trade CPU vs less fragmentation.

Sam: make compression opt-in. need bookkeeping so first access decompresses transparently and we track decompressed size cost.

Sara: flags: ATOMIC, FORWARDING, COMPRESS. default = ATOMIC+no-compress. will document semantics.

Mike: failure modes? what if forwarding map grows or TTL expires while pointers still in use?

Sara: fallback: if forwarding TTL expires and access occurs, page fault handler triggers fallback path that blocks until the move completes or copies back. worst-case user pays a stall; we'll instrument.

Jia: and quota/tenant isolation? moves should not leak pointers across tenants; forwarding map must be tenant-scoped and scrubbed on move failure.

Sara: yes tenant-scoped forwarding entries; scrub on abort/commit.

Sam: implementation note: keep fast-path checks branchless and cacheline-friendly. forwarding map in separate slow-path table.

Leo: one more: expose diagnostics API to list in-flight moves, tokens, and per-move progress for support tooling.

Sara: will add /internal/moves endpoint gated behind admin flag.

Mike: ok. please write RFC: include API, journal format, metrics, test plan, and perf targets (reduce 99.9p tail by X ms on heavy KV workloads).

Sara: will draft RFC & PR by EOD Friday. owner: Sara. action items: Mike scribe tests, Sam add telemetry hooks, Jia design journal format, Leo review allocator integration.

dev-bot: note: include CI flakiness guard for GPU tests (timeout bump + retry).
